Subject: Quantified economics & service layering — post-demo clarifications

Thanks for a great demo yesterday — quick recap with the specific numbers we discussed so we’re aligned before I hand this over to pricing and CS for the pilot scoping. High level: AsterHealth is evaluating a month-long pilot across patient messaging (chat), clinical search/embeddings, and a small rerank pass for triage results.

Key numbers you gave on the call (please flag anything I got wrong):
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~350k user requests / month (mix of short chats and system prompts)
- Average tokens per chat request: ~420 tokens (prompt+response)
- Projected total token volume: ~150M tokens / month (this is peak; conservative baseline for pilot: 20–30M tokens/month)
- Budget range for pilot: $15k–$30k total for the month (finance wants an approximate $/1M token target to evaluate)

Model mix we talked through (pilot target split):
- Chat (conversational): 62% of token volume — primary agent responses and summaries
- Embeddings (semantic search + rerank input): 28% of token volume — indexed chunks + encode calls
- Rerank/light re-ranker: 10% of token volume — short rerank prompts after retrieval

Unit economics target: you mentioned a target around $700–$950 per 1M tokens for pilot pricing bands depending on SLA and routing (region and reserved v. hosted). If AsterHealth needs a hard number for procurement, we should propose a conservative target and then show optional optimizations that lower per-M token costs.

Immediate asks / next steps from Redwood: 
1) Ben — can you confirm recommended pilot pricing tiles based on the 20–30M baseline and the route options (hosted standard / hosted optimized / dedicated burst)?
2) Marcus — tech follow-up: can you validate expected average latency targets for the chat path at the token sizes above and confirm which model variants (quantized v. fp16) we’d suggest for pilot?
3) Aisha — can you confirm who on procurement should receive the high-level cost worksheet (cc’d procurement@asterhealth.com?) and whether the pilot needs a separate DPA/POI before we start?

Attachments: I’ll attach the scoping worksheet and a short pricing tile PDF in the next message.

Thanks — Grace

Thanks Grace — quick pricing orientation from my side before Marcus and Monica scope the pilot technical/operational bits. High level thoughts aligned to the numbers above:
- For pilot baseline (20–30M tokens/month): propose three tiered tiles:
  * Hosted Standard: $1,050 / 1M tokens (no reserved capacity, best-effort routing)
  * Hosted Optimized: $820 / 1M tokens (batching + prefix cache optimizations enabled)
  * Dedicated Burst (small reserved pool): $640 / 1M tokens (committed short-term capacity + prioritized routing)
- Given Aisha’s budget band ($15k–$30k), the ranges map approximately to:
  * Hosted Standard -> covers ~14–28M tokens (at $1,050)
  * Hosted Optimized -> covers ~18–36M tokens (at $820)
  * Dedicated Burst -> covers ~23–46M tokens (at $640)

Ben’s ask: if procurement needs a single target $/1M to approve the pilot quickly, we recommend proposing the Hosted Optimized tile at $820 / 1M with a one-month pilot commitment and a rollback to Hosted Standard if SLAs aren’t met. That hits the middle of the customer’s stated range and leaves room to demonstrate optimizations that lower costs.

I’ll draft the pricing tiles as a short PDF and attach. Also: Marcus, can you confirm whether enabling prefix caching for patient messages could realistically shave 10–15% off token costs in steady state?

—Ben

Thanks Grace and Ben — appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Volume sanity: 150M is our upper bound if we scale quickly; pilot should be scoped for 25M tokens as conservative.
- Model split for pilot: we prefer to lock the embedding model family (encode-only) to a mid-size quantized variant and keep chat models on a lower-latency variant even if slightly more expensive. Proposed pilot split we can commit to:
  * Chat responses: 60%
  * Embeddings (encode-only): 30%
  * Rerank (short form): 10%
- Target $/1M: procurement asked for a firm target of $800 / 1M for initial approval. If Redwood can provide that as a pilot band (Host Optimized or Dedicated Burst with a short-term commit), we can move quickly.
- Compliance: procurement wants a SOC2 snapshot and data-retention notes before signature. Monica, could you share that doc if available?

Procurement contact: procurement@asterhealth.com (please include a short pricing worksheet and a one-page security snapshot).

Best,

Thanks Aisha — looping in the exact artifacts and next-step plan. Attached to this thread: pilot-scoping-sheet.xlsx (requested inputs prefilled), redwood-pricing-tiles.pdf (Ben's tiles), and security-qa-snapshot.pdf (SOC2 + retention bullets).

Operational notes for the pilot and internal owners: 
- Pilot duration: 30 days after sign-off.
- Success metrics: latency P95 under 600ms for chat path, embedding throughput of 300 qps sustained, cost variance < 15% vs estimate.
- Model variants recommended for pilot:
  * Chat: rdx-chat-v2-small (quantized, low-latency) — primary route
  * Embeddings: rdx-embed-meduim-q4 — encode-only quantized variant
  * Rerank: rdx-rank-lite — short context cheap pass
- Expected per-model volume split (pilot commitment): Chat 60% / Embeddings 30% / Rerank 10% (matches Aisha’s note).
- Optimization levers to reduce $/1M during pilot: prefix caching, request-level aggregation, and a lightweight on-request rerank threshold to limit rerank calls. Marcus to validate expected % savings for each lever by EOD Friday.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Ben: finalize pricing PDF for procurement with the $800 / 1M pilot tile and the Hosted Optimized fallback (ETA: today EOD).
2) Marcus: provide latency/throughput verification and caching savings estimate (ETA: Fri 19 Nov).
3) Grace: confirm procurement contact and send one-page pilot MOU (ETA: Tue 16 Nov afternoon).

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if procurement wants an immediate walkthrough.
